summary.text: 水 is a whole-character picture of flowing water: early forms show a central current with marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts flowing water as a whole, rather than combining separate components. Oracle-bone forms vary in their side marks, while bronze and Warring States forms retain the water image.

history.text: The cited oracle-bone examples use 水 for water or flooding. The curated oracle-script and Western Zhou bronze-script forms illustrate the flowing-water motif; both are modern vector redrawings, not artifact photographs.

The Han-era Shuowen account combines a gloss with a cosmological explanation of water’s direction and yin-yang qualities. That historical explanation is separate from the graph’s pictorial formation; 凖 is also analyzed there as a phonetic gloss.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 水 to write the different word 乞, “request.” This is a proposed sound-based reuse of the sign, not a change in the meaning of 水; the historical sound match remains unverified.

uncertainties.text: One reported oracle-bone verbal use is disputed: proposed readings involve leveling land with water or washing a temple. Its connection, if any, to the noun “water” is unresolved.
The supplied reconstructions and proposed comparisons for the spoken word 水 remain unresolved here and do not establish a phonetic component in the graph.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone examples; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: The cited oracle-bone examples are reported as uses for water or flooding; “water” is also given as the character’s basic meaning.
The common current meaning is “water.” Other glosses include liquid, lotion, and juice, but their chronology is not established.
The compound 水準 is reported with the meaning “leveling instrument.” This use is not dated in the cited account.
水準 is also reported with the abstract sense “standard” or “level.” Its development from the instrument sense is described, but neither stage is dated in the cited account.
A bronze inscription is reported to use 水 to write the different word 乞, “request.” This graph borrowing does not show that “water” developed into “request.”
One reported oracle-bone use has been read as a verb involving leveling ground with water or washing a temple. Its reading and connection to the noun “water” are unresolved.

developments.text: The abstract sense “standard” or “level” is reported as developing from the leveling-instrument sense, though the transition is not dated.

The graph was reportedly reused to write 乞, “request,” on the proposed basis that the words sounded alike or similarly; their historical sound match is not established, and no reconstruction comparison for both words is supported here.

limitations.text: The cited account does not date individual oracle-bone examples or the stages of 水準. The disputed verbal use’s relation to the ordinary water noun is also unresolved.

overview.text: 水 pictures flowing water, with a central current and marks for droplets. It was also reportedly reused to write 乞, “request,” on a proposed sound match that remains unverified.
